title: Implementation plan document
description: Implementation-tier (I) registry document (doc 11 §6): the project's decomposition into work packages (WP-NNNN) that downstream specifications are written against. Authored by planning agents from tier A. Canonical form is YAML (`implementation-plan.yaml`), wholly structured; prose fields are markdown strings. The validator projects the file to {meta, data} and validates the projection. Extends the common envelope (doc 11 §4) and constrains it to the implementation-plan type. Authoring guidance: carve the build into independent packages with disjoint file leases (02 §2) so phases can swarm; ground every package upstream via links.realizes into a contract or requirement (rule T4).

type.description: Document type discriminator; fixed to `implementation-plan` so the validator selects this schema.

data.description: Structured work-package plan. The only content beyond the envelope; this document has no narrative `sections`.

packages.description: The work packages this plan decomposes the build into, one record each. At least one package must be present. Each is an independently citable implementation item (WP-NNNN) that exactly one specification is written against (doc 11 §6, §7 T4).

workPackage.description: A single work package: a self-contained unit of build work with an exclusive file lease, a token budget, and an upstream grounding. Independence between packages is established here at planning time by disjoint `file_leases` so a phase can fan them out as a swarm (02 §2, 04 §7).

id.description: Stable work-package identifier in the form WP-NNNN, e.g. WP-0007 (doc 11 §3 grammar). Unique within this document; the join key downstream specifications cite (exactly one SPEC per WP, T4) and other packages reference via `depends_on`. Never reused or renumbered once assigned.

title.description: Short human-readable name for the package, e.g. `Billing service handlers` or `Order store migration`. Names the deliverable, not the activity.

scope.description: Markdown statement of what this package builds and, where it sharpens the boundary, what it explicitly does not. The contract the implementing agent works to: enough to plan and verify the work, bounded by the file leases below.

file_leases.description: The package's exclusive write claim: an array of file path glob patterns (e.g. `internal/billing/**`, `proto/billing/v1/*.proto`) this package may write. A FileLease (02 §2). At least one glob is required. Leases MUST be disjoint across concurrent packages — overlapping leases are a planning error caught here, not a merge conflict caught later (02 §2).

items.description: A single file path glob string the package claims write access to, relative to the project repo root. Globs may use `*` and `**`.

depends_on.description: Work packages that must complete before this one can start: an array of WP-NNNN references within this document. Sequencing only; independence (disjoint leases) is separate. Omit or leave empty for packages with no predecessors. References MUST resolve within this plan and MUST NOT be cyclic (corpus-checked).

items.description: A WP-NNNN reference to another package in this plan.

budget.description: The package's token budget and the policy for what happens when it is exceeded.

tokens.description: The token budget allotted to building this package, as a positive integer. Sizes the package and bounds the implementing agent's run.

escalation.description: Markdown statement of the escalation policy when the token budget is exhausted: what the implementing agent does next (e.g. re-plan, split the package, request human review, hand back). Describes the policy, not a single threshold number.

links.description: Typed upstream edges for this package (doc 11 §3). MUST carry at least one `realizes` edge — every work package realizes a contract (CTR-NNNN) or requirement (REQ-NNNN) it serves (rule T4). The presence of `realizes` is required here; that the target resolves to a CTR/REQ is the corpus-level T4 check. Use `refines` for same-tier elaboration. Direction is upstream only; reverse edges are derived by tooling, never written.

realizes.description: The upstream contracts and/or requirements this package serves. At least one reference is required (rule T4). Each entry is a CTR-NNNN or REQ-NNNN item id; corpus validation confirms it resolves and points upstream (T1, T2).
